title: Relational continuity with a family physician and unplanned admissions in older adults: a systematic review
abstract: Objective: to estimate the association between relational continuity with a family physician and unplanned admissions in adults aged 65 and over, in studies that adjust for illness severity, and the effect of interventions designed to raise continuity. Methods: systematic review with severity-adjusted pooling and intervention studies reported separately. Results will follow the full search.
introduction: Continuity is valued by patients and physicians, and several studies link it to fewer admissions. Because sicker patients see more physicians, unadjusted associations overstate any benefit, and few studies have raised continuity on purpose.
methods: Three bibliographic databases are searched from 2000 with forward citation checking, and every lead from the preliminary scan is checked. Two reviewers screen independently and a third resolves disagreements. Only estimates adjusted for morbidity or prior use are pooled; intervention studies and waiting times are tabulated separately.
results: The full search has not been run; the preliminary search returned two records.
discussion: To be written against the network's decision on personal lists. The discussion will weigh any association against the waiting-time cost shown by intervention studies.
limitations: English-language studies from high-income systems only; residual confounding by severity in included studies.
